doctrines.title: AI layer integrity
doctrines.statement: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and names sections that exist, the local half is ignored by git with nothing under it tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai path.
doctrines.summary: The repository's AI layer is real: the manifest declares a format this executable reads and every section it names exists, the checkout-local half is ignored by git and nothing under it is tracked, and no project data remains under the pre-.ai .majordomus/ path.

doctrines.title: Checkpoint freshness
doctrines.statement: A task whose newest checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported as stale, and the report does not stop the work.
doctrines.summary: A task whose last checkpoint is older than its profile's interval is reported, not stopped.

doctrines.title: Layout integrity
doctrines.statement: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.
doctrines.summary: The directories the durable commands write into are installed rather than created on first use.

doctrines.title: Ledger integrity
doctrines.statement: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event.
doctrines.summary: Every line of the append-only ledger is a well-formed event; the one durable record nothing else can reconstruct stays readable.

doctrines.title: Policy completeness
doctrines.statement: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries a default of its own.
doctrines.summary: Every policy value the code reads is declared in the skeleton policy, and no reader carries its own default for one.

doctrines.title: Bootstrap integrity
doctrines.statement: A person reaches the AI layer through README.md and AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.
doctrines.summary: The path from a human reader to the AI layer is unbroken — README.md names AGENTS.md, every generated instruction file points at .ai/README.md, and none of them carries a rule of its own.

doctrines.title: Catalogue integrity
doctrines.statement: Every use case and application names only commands, rules and claims that exist, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.
doctrines.summary: Every use case and application describes the tool in terms the tool has — each command, doctrine and claim it names exists, and the two catalogues reference each other in both directions.

doctrines.title: Context integrity
doctrines.statement: Every context document under the layer carries the context contract with a unique identity, every reference in it resolves within its ancestor chain, no final document is superseded, and the effective context for any path is computed from the tree root down in one deterministic order.
doctrines.summary: The scoped context documents under the AI layer carry the context contract, compose into one deterministic chain for every path, and a tree that does not validate resolves nothing.

doctrines.title: Policy integrity
doctrines.statement: The policy and every profile parse, declare a supported version, and carry no key the schema does not define.
doctrines.summary: The policy and every profile parse, declare version 1, and carry no key the schema does not define.

doctrines.title: Blocker resolution
doctrines.statement: No task is accepted as completed while any question on the branch is unresolved.
doctrines.summary: No task can be completed while any question on this branch is unresolved; it can still be finished as blocked, partial, no_match or failed.

doctrines.title: Decision records
doctrines.statement: Every recorded decision carries the task, the head and the reason, so the worker who needs it can find it.
doctrines.summary: Every entry in decisions.md carries the task, the head and the reason, so a decision can be found by the worker who needs it.

doctrines.title: Dependency graph integrity
doctrines.statement: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue executes ahead of a dependency that is not done.
doctrines.summary: The issue dependency graph is acyclic, every edge names an issue that exists, and no issue is executing ahead of a dependency that is not done.

doctrines.title: The command surface is declared and reconciled
doctrines.statement: The command registry is authority for what a command means and the dispatcher for what runs; neither derives from the other, and doctor refuses a command present in one and absent from the other, in either direction.
doctrines.summary: Every command the binary dispatches is described by the shipped registry, every command the registry declares public is dispatched, and a command is public exactly when the usage text lists it.

doctrines.title: Doctrine wiring integrity
doctrines.statement: Every enforced rule resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test that CI runs; and every validator is declared by a rule.
doctrines.summary: Every doctrine in this registry resolves to a validator that exists, is reached from every command it names, propagates failure, is proved by a test, and is run by CI — and every validator in the source is declared here.

doctrines.title: Enforcement wiring
doctrines.statement: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher executes, without a swallowed exit code.
doctrines.summary: Every enforcement the policy declares is invoked by the hook it names, from a file the dispatcher will actually execute, without swallowing the exit code.

doctrines.title: Every public command is exercised and refuted
doctrines.statement: Coverage is owed to every public command from the moment it is registered; a case declares which commands it exercises and which failure modes it asserts, and a public command that no case declares in both layers is a failure.
doctrines.summary: Every public command has a behavioural test and a negative test, computed from the registry and the coverage each case declares about itself rather than from a list someone maintains.

doctrines.title: Handover integrity
doctrines.statement: The record resolver reports the handover for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never skipped silently.
doctrines.summary: The resolver runs and reports either the record for this worktree and branch or its clean absence; a malformed record is never silently skipped, and a record describing a history this checkout no longer has is reported.

doctrines.title: Note integrity
doctrines.statement: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and never a transcript.
doctrines.summary: Every outcome needs a note carrying the sections that outcome requires, and no transcript.

doctrines.title: Profile requirements
doctrines.principle: Escalate capability and effort only when justified
doctrines.statement: A profile may require more than the shared contract, and finish refuses a completed outcome that lacks it.
doctrines.summary: A profile may demand more than the shared contract — a regression test, a decision record — and finish refuses without it.

doctrines.title: Project model integrity
doctrines.statement: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.
doctrines.summary: Every milestone and issue file parses, carries the id its filename claims, and contains no key nobody reads.

doctrines.title: Projection integrity
doctrines.statement: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the content it declares, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.
doctrines.summary: Every generated instruction file exists, matches the stamp it carries, and is never silently overwritten after a hand edit.

doctrines.title: Context budget
doctrines.statement: The always-loaded projection stays within its budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits its own budget.
doctrines.summary: The always-loaded projection stays within its line budget, every reference in it resolves, it states no count that will go stale, and the assembled context fits the builder's own budget.

doctrines.title: Prompt capture is proven, or reported unavailable
doctrines.statement: Prompt capture is either wired below the model and proven by execution, or reported as unavailable; the archive is never committed, and a record carries the closed field set and no model output.
doctrines.summary: A repository that declares prompt capture has it wired below the model and proven by running it; the archive stays ignored and untracked, and every record carries the person's prompt and nothing the model said.

doctrines.title: Prompt integrity
doctrines.statement: Every reusable prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.
doctrines.summary: Every repository-local prompt asset renders, and every token in it is one the renderer knows.

doctrines.title: Questions store integrity
doctrines.statement: Every entry in the questions store parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.
doctrines.summary: Every entry in open-questions.md parses, because a gate that cannot read an entry can be bypassed by mistyping one.

doctrines.title: Retention caps
doctrines.statement: The ledger, the handovers and the checkpoints stay under the caps the policy sets.
doctrines.summary: The ledger and the handover directory stay under the caps the policy sets, so durable state does not grow without bound.

doctrines.title: The roadmap is a projection, never a document
doctrines.statement: No document is a second authority for the roadmap; a hand-written table can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.
doctrines.summary: No document is a second authority for the roadmap. While a hand-written roadmap table exists, it can neither list a version no milestone declares nor hide one the model does.

doctrines.title: Rule package integrity
doctrines.statement: The vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every effective rule resolves with its dependencies, no two rules claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.
doctrines.summary: The repository's effective rule set is real: the vendored baseline matches its manifest file for file, every rule resolves with its dependencies and no two claim one identity, and no project rule reuses the vendored namespace.

doctrines.title: Scope integrity
doctrines.statement: Work outside the paths a task claimed is not accepted as that task's work.
doctrines.summary: A task touches only the paths it claimed; work found elsewhere is not accepted as done.

doctrines.title: Skill integrity
doctrines.statement: A skill is canonical data under the skills section; it is valid against the skill schema, its id is its directory, its body carries the sections a reader relies on, and every reference it makes resolves.
doctrines.summary: Every skill the repository declares parses against the skill contract, names the directory it lives in, carries its sections, and every skill or example it refers to exists.

doctrines.title: State consistency
doctrines.statement: A task record is trusted only while it still describes this checkout: same branch, HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.
doctrines.summary: The task record still describes this checkout — same branch, and HEAD at or ahead of the recorded commit.

doctrines.title: Task continuity
doctrines.statement: A task finished as partial or blocked leaves a handover record, not only a note section.
doctrines.summary: A task finished as partial or blocked should leave a handover record, not only a note section.

doctrines.title: Use-case coverage
doctrines.statement: A capability the policy requires coverage for is demonstrated by an executable use case, and a capability without one is a named gap.
doctrines.summary: Every public command, and every guaranteed claim and MCP tool the policy asks for, is named and run by at least one active use case whose scenario executes against the real tool; a gap is a failure or a report according to the policy, never silence.

doctrines.title: Verification integrity
doctrines.statement: A completed outcome requires a verification command that ran and exited zero, with its exit code and duration recorded.
doctrines.summary: Completion requires a verification command that actually ran and exited 0; its exit code and duration are recorded.
